E1.excerpt: In this work we performed first principles calculations integrated with implicit solvation at constant potentials to examine the detailed atomistic reaction mechanism of OER at the IrO2 (110) surface.

E2.excerpt: (no publication date is printed anywhere in the main text or SI; only reference-list years appear)

E3.excerpt: We compared the free energy of all possible positions of dissociated H2O and found both –OOH and –OH bonds prefer to form at the top O atoms

E4.excerpt: We chose IrO2 (110) surface because it has been shown theoretically to be the most stable surface similar to other rutile structures, TiO2 and RuO2.

E5.excerpt: We performed first principles calculations of IrO2 (110) surface with plane wave basis sets and GBRV ultrasoft pseudopotentials within the Quantum-Espresso package.

E6.excerpt: The overpotential corresponding to the current j 10mA/cm2 (lnj is -4.6) is 0.22 V, which is in good agreement with the experimental overpotential of 0.27±0.03 … 𝜂 is the overpotential for oxidizing H2O (the potential relative to NHE+1.23 eV)

note: Single model IrO2(110). The only value labeled overpotential (0.22 V) is a Tafel-derived kinetic overpotential from a microkinetic model, not a CHE result; SI gives raw ΔG steps and η only as a kinetic-rate parameter.

E1.excerpt: We demonstrate that dissimilar reaction mechanisms and limiting steps for the OER over IrO2(110) are obtained for different active surface configurations present on the IrO2 electrode.

E3.where: main: Methods, Computational hydrogen electrode approach
E3.excerpt: Free energies of reaction intermediates in the OER are obtained by applying the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) approach of Nørskov and coworkers

E4.excerpt: Rutile IrO2 is described by a (2 × 1) surface slab model along the (110) direction, and a 7 × 7 × 1 Γ-centered k-point mesh is applied

E5.excerpt: We model the OER over a (2 × 1) IrO2(110) surface by DFT calculations; all computational details can be found in section 1 of the SI.

E6.excerpt: This is the reason why we adopt the concept of Gmax(U) rather than the notion of ηTD in our mechanistic analysis … the limiting free-energy span is reconciled with *cus-OHot → *cus-Oot → *cus-OOHot → *cus + O2 due to the strong adsorption of the *OH intermediate

note: Multiple rutile IrO2(110) models/mechanisms (mononuclear, bifunctional, oxide, binuclear, Walden); all report only Gmax(U), a multi-step free-energy span explicitly distinguished from and used instead of the thermodynamic overpotential ηTD.
